name: editing_ruins_video
summary: An analytical video critique featuring an in-person conversational podcast interspersed with Premiere Pro timeline breakdowns and side-by-side edit comparisons. The visual rhythm balances steady conversational multi-cam dialogue with focused, illustrative B-roll case studies.

captions.notes: Captions primarily appear inside embedded documentary clips using legible white text with soft dark drop shadow.

headline.notes: Small lower-corner tags distinguish comparison clips ('Drew's Edit', 'Hayden's Edit') and bold section headers label editing concepts.

callouts.notes: Minimal line diagrams, directional motion arrows, and boxed overlays highlight visual focus points and pacing mechanics.

transitions.notes: Natural audio lead-ins (J/L cuts) connect podcast discussion to timeline demonstrations and archival footage.

end_screen.tone: Direct and educational call to masterclass and editing consultations.

rules: Switch to B-roll or NLE screen captures whenever a specific cut decision is critiqued
Label source comparison versions in the corner with clean pill tags
Preserve breathing room during serious topic explanations rather than over-compressing pauses
Use screen graphics like directional arrows and boxes to demonstrate gaze movement and eye-tracing
Support editing lessons with real project timeline views showing track stacking and audio layout
Maintain consistent multi-cam angles for podcast interview framing
Align B-roll motion vectors continuously across consecutive cuts for spatial cohesion
Switch between wide studio shot, individual host close-ups, and full-screen edit playback based on conversational flow.
Use picture-in-picture host reactions over footage when commentary directly references real-time visual beats.
Label distinct comparison versions clearly in the lower corner with consistent color and font branding.
Overlay compositing guides and eye-tracing targets to visualize editing feedback concretely.
Preserve natural conversational pacing without hyper-fast jump cutting during discussions.
avoid: Rapid-fire meme popups or cartoon sound effects during serious subject analysis
Unmotivated whip pans and flash transitions
Constant digital push-ins or zoom punches every few seconds
Flashy decorative transitions like 3D spins or cheesy screen wipes.
Overly aggressive zoom punches every few seconds.
Cluttered animated stickers that distract from footage analysis.
